sources.title: Gigabit capable broadband local indicator
sources.lines: indicator definition, Jan 2026 vintage and download notes
facts: The indicator measures the percentage of premises covered by a gigabit-capable service of 1,000 Mbit/s or more.
The observation vintage is January 2026 and the indicator was published on 13 May 2026.
The displayed geography is lower-tier or unitary authority.
Confidence intervals are not available for this indicator.
ONS warns that aggregation may create differences from other published figures.

sources.title: About this data – fixed coverage and full-fibre take-up (v2)
facts: The January 2026 snapshot collected orderable-service records from 52 fixed and 18 fixed-wireless providers.
Ofcom used AddressBase Premium and Islands Epoch 123 as its premises base.
Version 2 corrected duplicate postcode-area files for CW and MK and renamed 121 all-premises postcode files to revision 2.
Postcode-level files report gigabit-capable coverage but omit full-fibre coverage for commercial-confidentiality reasons.
Coverage, take-up, technology, geography and premises type must remain distinct fields.

sources.title: About this data – mobile coverage
facts: The four mobile network operators supplied coverage predictions with a reference date of 1 January 2026.
The files cover UK and nations, local authorities and parliamentary or devolved constituencies.
The local-authority file contains 361 rows and 154 coverage columns.
4G outdoor coverage uses a -105 dBm RSRP threshold and indoor or in-car uses -95 dBm.
5G High Confidence uses -110 dBm SS-RSRP while Very High Confidence uses -100 dBm.

sources.title: Mobile Matters research index and 2025 release
facts: The 2025 release analyses crowdsourced mobile data collected from October 2024 to March 2025.
It examines network technology, connection success, file transfer times, latency and speed distributions.
The results are compared by mobile network operator and location.
The research page separately publishes the report, chart data and an interactive report.
Measured performance in coverage areas must not be interpreted as universal geographic coverage.

sources.title: Mobile Matters 2025: crowdsourced mobile-network experience
facts: The report uses more than 120 million Opensignal datapoints collected in coverage areas.
Data from Apple iOS devices were excluded to preserve comparability with prior reports.
5G standalone represented 2% of 5G connection attempts in the measurement period.
Median file-download times were about 45% faster on 5G standalone than on 5G non-standalone.
The report explicitly separates real-world performance in coverage areas from coverage availability.

sources.title: Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy Early Process Evaluation collection
facts: The publication was released on 13 January 2025.
It provides an early process review of the GIS intervention.
The collection publishes both HTML and PDF versions of the report.
The evaluation focuses on delivery processes rather than measured service at individual premises.
Process findings require separation from operational coverage observations.

sources.title: Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy Intervention Early Process Evaluation
facts: The report assesses market engagement, intervention design, intervention-area development and OMR or public-review processes.
Early findings describe high network-provider participation in the OMR process.
All contracts tendered at the research point attracted network-provider submissions.
The report notes concerns about changed local-body responsibilities and internal data across interventions.
Evaluation findings are programme-process evidence and not exact UPRN service proof.

sources.title: Building Digital UK Annual Report and Accounts 2024 to 2025
facts: The annual report records that BDUK achieved its 95% UK geographic 4G target ahead of schedule.
It distinguishes Project Gigabit, Shared Rural Network, Hubs and voucher evaluation activity.
It reports continued use of independent evaluation and stakeholder research.
Corporate performance measures are programme-level outcomes rather than address-level availability.
Annual-report figures require preservation of reporting period and programme scope.

sources.title: Gigabit infrastructure subsidy guidance: wholesale open access network requirements
facts: The guidance applies wholesale network-access requirements to suppliers receiving GIS subsidy.
The subsidy-control requirements are legally separate from the communications regulatory framework.
Access requirements must be read alongside the scheme's pricing rules.
The guidance concerns contract and compliance design, not current retail availability.
Wholesale eligibility cannot be promoted to parcel service status.

sources.title: Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy guidance: transparency, monitoring and reporting
facts: The guidance was updated on 26 July 2024.
BDUK's National Competence Centre administers transparency requirements for the GIS scheme.
Transparency covers record keeping and publication of specified project information.
The document separates the responsibilities of BDUK, implementing bodies, local bodies and suppliers.
Published compliance information does not establish service availability at a premise.
